reply_text:
Re-proposing left the first run's proposals in the store, which would form cycles if both were applied. Fixing it so a re-run withdraws proposals that are no longer in the new set:There are now 17 proposals, each backed by a direct judgement. Next I'm testing apply, show and undo on the park pair:All of it works. After the merge, the old id resolves to the kept one and picks up its links. As of before the merge, and after the undo, the two memories are separate again. Committing:㊥ ("start with part 1") Part 1 is done: there are 17 merge proposals in the scratch store, and none have been applied. Committed as `b875fd3`.

㊢ (how it works) The 18 `restates` pairs fall into 14 groups. Each group keeps one memory and the others become aliases that point to it. Merging doesn't rewrite anything. A merge is a dated "A now resolves to B" edge, and queries follow it, so links, versions and sorries keep the ids they were written with. `show <id>` gives a memory's kept id, the memories merged into it, and every link, sorry and proposal touching any of them. `undo` reverses a merge.

㊩ (two problems, both fixed)
- **Which memory to keep.** My first rule kept the memory with the most inbound links. In the verification group, that left 2 of 3 merges resting on no direct judgement. The rule now prefers the memory judged a duplicate of the most others, and all 17 merges are backed by direct judgements.
- **Stale proposals.** Re-running `propose` left the first run's proposals in place, which would have created A→B and B→A cycles. A re-run now withdraws proposals that are no longer in the new set.

㊬ (checked) I tested on `park-needs-session-id` → `emacs-park-needs-session`. After applying, the old id resolved to the kept one and its link came along: 3 edges instead of 2. Asking as of before the merge still showed them separate, and `undo` restored the separate state. The unit tests (29 assertions), clj-kondo and the parenthesis check pass.

㊟ (the proposals; full list in `~/code/data/minus40/aliases-proposed.txt`) Most are the same lesson filed under two projects, for example:
- `bg-py-for-durable-jobs` ← `repl-seat-long-runs-use-bg-py`
- `never-git-stash-in-shared-futon-trees` ← `no-git-stash-in-shared-checkout`
- `verification-is-registered-not-rerun` ← three test-rerun rules

Some keep-choices are arguable. `emacs-park-needs-session` is kept over `park-needs-session-id`, even though the latter is the one in my home memory index, because the emacs one has more links.

🈸 (one decision) Applying merges is your call, either all of them or some. Exporting a merged set back to Claude's flat files would also mean deleting the alias files and rewriting `[[links]]` in other memories, so I've left that until merges are actually applied. Otherwise part 2, entities, is next.
